web_title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside the Silicon — Audio, HPMS & Real-World Devices
question: What exact chips does Cirrus Logic design across its Audio and High-Performance Mixed-Signal (HPMS) product lines, how has the revenue mix shifted, and what do its real-world customer deployments look like?

epigraph.quote: Every digital processor eventually runs into the messy physics of sound, motion, light, and battery voltage; the translator at that boundary owns the real estate.
epigraph.author: Analog & Mixed-Signal Design Principle

web_blocks.title: 2.1 One Operating Segment, Two Complementary Product Lines

web_blocks.html: Cirrus Logic reports one GAAP segment, but splits net sales into two clear lines: Audio Products and High-Performance Mixed-Signal (HPMS) Products [1]. Both lines share the same core tech: ultra-low-power analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog converters, built-in digital signal processing (DSP), and tight power control made on mature-to-mid-node CMOS silicon [1][3]. In fiscal 2026 (ended March 28, 2026), total sales hit $1,997.38 million (+5.3% YoY). Audio brought $1,159.93 million (58.1% of sales) and HPMS brought $837.45 million (41.9%) [1]. That shift kept going in H1 FY2027 (six months ended September 26, 2026). HPMS grew 11.1% YoY to $455.64 million (44.7% of sales), while Audio edged up 0.9% YoY to $563.54 million (55.3%) [2][4].

web_blocks.caption: Cirrus Logic: Audited Product-Line Revenue Disaggregation (FY2022 – H1 FY2027)
web_blocks.takeaway: Over the past four and a half years, Audio has acted as a steady ~$1.1B–$1.2B cash cow. Virtually all net sales growth came from HPMS rising from 33.4% of sales in FY2022 to 44.7% in H1 FY2027 [1][2][9].

web_blocks.title: 2.2 Audio Products: 22nm Smart Codecs, Boosted Amplifiers & SoundWire PC Silicon

web_blocks.html: The Audio line rests on two main chip types: smart audio codecs and boosted Class-D speaker amplifiers. It also includes general-market DACs, ADCs, and pro-audio or auto codecs [1][3]. In flagship phones, Cirrus Logic recently moved its top buyer to a custom 22-nanometer smart codec paired with a new custom boosted amp [3]. Moving from 55nm to 22nm packs far more onboard DSP power into a tiny power budget. It runs always-on voice offload, active noise control, and spatial sound without waking the main processor [3]. Better still, custom phone audio sockets last a long time. In Q2 FY2027, management noted that prior custom codecs and boosted amps shipped for five and six years, giving multi-year sales visibility once qualified [3]. That long socket life matters for cash returns. Upfront R&D is paid back over five or six full product cycles rather than a single season [3]. It also gives Cirrus Logic time to co-develop the next chip node before the prior part rolls off [1][3].

Beyond phones, Audio leads Cirrus Logic's push into Windows and AI laptops [3][15]. For years, PC makers used legacy High Definition Audio (HDA) codecs led by Realtek Semiconductor. As thin laptops moved to the newer MIPI SoundWire (v1.2 / SDCA) bus to save board space and battery life, Cirrus launched its PC CS42L43 SmartHIFI codec and scalable CS35L56 boosted smart amps [15][16]. The CS42L43 fits in a 13 mm² chip-scale package and cuts power draw by up to 50% vs. older chips. It also plugs right into Microsoft's ACX audio framework and mainline Linux kernel drivers [15][17][19]. In Q2 FY2027, management noted a new six-speaker PC on NVIDIA's RTX Spark platform using Cirrus amps and codec. It also taped out its second-gen smart codec for AI PCs [3].

web_blocks.title: 2.3 High-Performance Mixed-Signal (HPMS): Camera Controllers, Haptics & Power ICs

web_blocks.html: HPMS is Cirrus Logic's main content-growth engine. Sales rose from $594.33 million in FY2022 to $837.45 million in FY2026 (+8.9% 4-year CAGR), then sped up to +11.1% YoY in H1 FY2027 [1][2][9]. Instead of selling generic catalog analog parts, Cirrus applies its closed-loop control IP across four specific areas [1][3]:

items: Closed-Loop Camera Controllers: Launched in fall 2020 and now across three shipped gens, these chips run autofocus voice-coil motors, optical image stabilization (OIS), and sensor-shift moves with sub-micron precision [3]. In Q2 FY2027, third-gen attach rates rose on new phones, and Cirrus taped out its fourth-gen camera chip for CY2028 [3].
Haptic & Sensing Drivers: Low-latency linear resonant actuator (LRA) drivers create crisp clicks in phones (replacing physical buttons) and solid-state haptic touchpads in thin laptops [1][3].

Battery, Charging & Smart Power ICs: Power and battery ICs include a new custom smart power IC in work for 3D-sensing (FaceID) at its top buyer. The October 2026 INVENTVM deal adds battery-monitoring IP as well [3][7].

General-Market Precision Converters: New non-phone HPMS chips target smart utility meters (analog front-end parts sampling in Q2 FY2027) and industrial imaging (first production orders won in Q2 FY2027) [3].

web_blocks.title: 2.4 Concrete End-to-End Customer Examples: Inside a Smartphone and an AI Laptop

web_blocks.html: Two late-2026 devices show how Cirrus Logic works in practice. Example 1: A Flagship Smartphone Bill of Materials. Suppose you shoot 4K steady video, feel a silent haptic tap, and take a speaker call. Five or more Cirrus Logic chips run together behind the scenes [1][3]. The custom 22nm smart codec converts audio from MEMS mics, cuts wind noise, and routes sound on tiny power [3]. Two custom boosted Class-D amps step up battery voltage to drive micro-speakers loud without burning the coils [3]. At the same time, the closed-loop haptic driver fires crisp pulses to mimic a real click. The third-gen camera chip tunes OIS and lens focus in real time [3]. Because each task sits right where battery voltage meets heat, sound, and motion, weak silicon hurts device quality at once.

Example 2: A Thin Windows AI Laptop (e.g., Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon / X9 or Dell Commercial Ultrabook). Sub-1-kilogram Windows 11 AI laptops leave almost no room for speaker chambers [15]. Swapping legacy HDA audio for Cirrus Logic's MIPI SoundWire CS42L43/CS42L45 codec and two to six CS35L56 boosted smart amps cuts audio PCB area by over 50%. It also drives louder sound with rattle control and unifies Windows ACX drivers across Intel Core Ultra, AMD, and ARM/NVIDIA chips [3][15][18]. Still, keep the scale in view. Despite wins at top PC OEMs (Lenovo, Dell, HP, ASUS), PC sales remain a small slice of revenue. In fact, PC sales fell quarter-on-quarter in Q2 FY2027 due to PC memory shortages and delayed model launches [2][3]. For investors, the takeaway from both hardware stacks is clear. Inside flagship phones, Cirrus Logic sells multi-chip bundles at massive volume [1][3]. Inside thin Windows AI laptops, the technical win is real, yet total revenue scale still trails far behind the core smartphone engine [2][3].

web_blocks.title: The Core Paradox of Cirrus Logic's Product Mix
paragraphs: Product mix is broadening—HPMS rose from 33.4% of sales in FY2022 to 44.7% in H1 FY2027 [2][9]. Yet buyer mix went the other way. Apple grew from 79% of sales in FY2022 to 91% in FY2026 and 93% in Q2 FY2027 [1][2][10].

The reason is simple. Most HPMS wins (camera chips, haptics, and new 3D-sensing power ICs) sit inside the same top smartphone buyer. Investors must separate content-per-device growth (strong) from true customer breadth (still unproven at scale).

book_paragraphs: To understand what Cirrus Logic actually sells, forget abstract semiconductor jargon for a moment and picture the physical boundary between a computer's digital brain and the real world. Inside your smartphone or laptop, the main processor thinks purely in binary ones and zeros. Yet the world you and I live in is stubbornly analog: sound waves vibrating through air, tiny camera lenses shifting by fractions of a millimeter to cancel hand tremor, haptic motors mimicking the crisp click of a physical button, and lithium-ion batteries fluctuating in voltage as they drain.

Cirrus Logic builds the precision mixed-signal translators that live right at that messy physical boundary. While the company reports as a single operating segment, management splits revenue into two clear buckets: Audio Products and High-Performance Mixed-Signal, or HPMS. In fiscal 2026, total sales reached $1.997 billion, with Audio contributing $1.16 billion—about 58 percent—and HPMS contributing $837 million, or 42 percent. By the first half of fiscal 2027, HPMS had climbed even further to nearly 45 percent of total sales, growing 11 percent year over year while Audio hummed along essentially flat.

Think of Audio as the steady cash cow and HPMS as the content-expansion engine. Inside the Audio bucket sit two flagship technologies: smart audio codecs and boosted speaker amplifiers. In recent smartphone cycles, Cirrus Logic migrated its custom smart codec down to a 22-nanometer manufacturing process. That shrink matters because it packs far more digital signal processing power into a tiny, ultra-low-power footprint—letting the phone listen for voice commands, cancel background noise, and route high-fidelity sound without waking up the battery-draining main processor. Even better, once a custom audio codec or boosted amplifier wins a socket inside a flagship smartphone platform, it tends to stay there for a long time. Management disclosed that its prior generations of custom codecs and amplifiers shipped for five and six years straight.

book_subsections.title: Walking Through Two Real-World Devices
paragraphs: Let's make this concrete by opening up two everyday machines you might have on your desk right now. First, pick up a modern flagship smartphone. When you take a video while walking down the street, tap a virtual button that feels uncannily like a mechanical switch, and then play a song out loud from speakers barely thicker than a coin, you are experiencing a coordinated orchestra of Cirrus Logic silicon. The 22-nanometer smart codec cleans up your voice across multiple microphones. Two boosted Class-D amplifiers step up the battery voltage to drive the micro-speakers at maximum loudness while constantly sensing coil temperature so they never distort or blow out. A closed-loop haptic driver fires a crisp, millisecond-accurate vibration pulse to your thumb. And inside the camera module, Cirrus Logic's third-generation camera controller makes thousands of microscopic real-time adjustments to stabilize the lens and lock focus. Management has already taped out its fourth-generation camera controller for calendar 2028 production, plus a new custom smart power IC aimed at 3D-sensing facial recognition.

Now open a modern ultrathin Windows AI laptop—say, a sub-kilogram Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon or a premium Dell ultrabook. For twenty years, PC makers bought cheap, off-the-shelf High Definition Audio codecs from Realtek. But as laptops became as thin as smartphones, OEMs began shifting to a sleeker standard called MIPI SoundWire. Cirrus Logic saw its opening and launched the CS42L43 SmartHIFI codec paired with its CS35L56 boosted smart amplifiers. Together, they cut audio board space by more than half, trim codec power draw by up to 50 percent, and let OEMs scale from two to six speakers—as seen in a newly launched six-speaker PC running on NVIDIA's RTX Spark platform—using a unified Windows software driver.

book_subsections.title: The Crucial Distinction: Product Mix vs. Customer Mix
paragraphs: Here is the subtle trap that trips up casual observers of Cirrus Logic, and I want you to spot it immediately. If you only look at the product-line table, you see a textbook diversification story: HPMS rose from 33 percent of revenue in fiscal 2022 to nearly 45 percent in the first half of fiscal 2027. You might assume the company is rapidly outgrowing its dependence on smartphones.

Look one layer deeper, however, and you see the exact opposite trend in customer concentration. Over that very same span, Apple's share of Cirrus Logic's total revenue climbed from 79 percent in fiscal 2022 to 91 percent in fiscal 2026—and reached 93 percent in the September 2026 quarter. Why? Because the vast majority of Cirrus Logic's HPMS growth—camera controllers, haptics, and emerging 3D-sensing power ICs—was won inside Apple's own devices, while PC laptops, smart utility meters, and industrial imaging sensors remain tiny relative to a two-billion-dollar revenue base. In fact, PC sales actually dipped sequentially in Q2 FY27 as memory shortages delayed several OEM laptop launches. So Cirrus Logic is undeniably succeeding at winning more silicon real estate per smartphone; what it has not yet proven is that its non-smartphone markets can move the needle on their own.

book_subsections.title: Why Smartphone Processors Don't Just Swallow These Chips
paragraphs: If you are thinking like a sharp skeptic, a very fair question should pop into your head right now: if modern smartphone processors are built on miraculous 3-nanometer silicon packing tens of billions of transistors, why doesn't the main processor simply swallow Cirrus Logic's audio amplifier, haptic driver, and camera controller onto one giant chip?

The answer comes down to basic electrical physics. Leading-edge 3-nanometer digital transistors are optimized to switch billions of times a second at tiny voltages—under one volt. By contrast, driving a physical micro-speaker loudly, firing a haptic vibration motor, or moving a camera lens assembly requires stepping up battery voltage cleanly and handling real physical current without generating electrical noise or heat. If you try to cram a high-voltage boosted amplifier or a precision analog-to-digital converter onto a cutting-edge digital processor die, the analog circuitry takes up huge, expensive wafer area and picks up digital switching noise. It is far cheaper, quieter, and more power-efficient to keep those mixed-signal functions on dedicated 22-nanometer to 90-nanometer specialty chips.

That exact physics advantage is also what gives Cirrus Logic a credible technical bridge into adjacent markets. Beyond laptops, management began sampling new analog front-end chips for smart utility meters in the September 2026 quarter, secured its first production orders for industrial imaging components, and acquired Italy's INVENTVM to target piezoelectric audio and battery power in next-generation AI wearables. None of these general-market lines will replace smartphone revenue tomorrow, but each one exploits the same core skill: translating messy analog reality into crisp digital signals on a microscopic power budget.

book_callouts.title: Mentor Check: Content Growth Is Not Customer Diversification
book_callouts.text: Always separate two questions when auditing a component supplier: 'Are they winning more chips per device?' and 'Are they winning more customers?' For Cirrus Logic, the answer to the first question is a resounding yes—HPMS is nearly 45% of sales. The answer to the second question is still no—one customer drives over 90% of the top line.
